Hello Guys,
Yesterday evening we ended up in a quite weird situation.
Foreword: The intruder bag had 2 breeder tokens plus all the others token (queen, blank, larva and adults).
One of the guy got a larva and then a creeper spawned out of him. Then through an event card the creeper became a breeder.
On another encounter we picked a breeder token, now only one breeder token remains in the bag (plus all the others).
Both the breeders were engaged in combat.
Another encounter happens I a different room and we draw another breeder.
Now, only two breeders miniatures exist and both were already engaged in combat.
What happens in that case? Do they flee? An adult spawn? The queen spawn? Nothing spawn?
According to the rules, that only talks about adults by the way, we should remove all that type of minis that are not engaged in combat and resolve the encounter by placing a mini in the room where the encounter happened.
But in our case both minis were engaged. What to do? Did we miss something?
Thank you for your clarifications!

How did you manage to get two Breeder tokens into a bag?
If I remember correctly, you'd need to evolve one Creeper from the bag, get new Creeper from your friend's chest, evolve him into Breeder and make him retreat into a technical corridor.
If after all that you still manage to get another Creeper from your another friend's chest and evolve him too - you need to check your calendar to know how much days you were playing =)
But if your situation is legit, I'd say nothing happens same as for Adult's rule.
You can think about it like if you have TWO Breeders on the board and another one in the bag, you deserve a little break =)
Anyway, the bag starts with only one Creeper and none of the Breeders, did you play like that?

Daniel Ebeck

You should not be starting with the Breeders on the bag. As per pg6 point 10

Rune M @Rulebook

Take the Intruder bag and put the following Intruder tokens
inside: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults.
Then, add 1 additional Adult Intruder token for each player taking
part in the game.

So Breeders only get added to the bag through drawing a Creeper in the Bag Development phase.
We have the unused tokens stored in "stock" off to the side, away from the action. When we draw a token from the bag for an Encounter, we place the token on the Intruder Board to keep it safe. If the Intruder flees, it can go back from the board and into the bag and if it is killed, it goes back to the main "stock".

I guess it is 'possible' to run out of minis - but not likley.
You would need the starting creeper to turn into a breeder, then 2 players to die which turn them into creepers, then the 'all intruders leave board' card (whatever its called) to come up (so you have 3 creepers in the bag), then the 3 creepers to be upgraded to breeders, then all 3 breeders to be drawn. Then you would be out of minis.
In the event you run out of minis, I would house play it you take the next intruder in scale - so for breeders, take the queen, if the queen is out, take the king (when it arrives), and if you cant do that, everybody noise rolls???

More on Contamination cards – see below.

# CONTAMINATION CARDS

In addition to Wounds, Characters may get Contamination cards (for example as the result of some Intruder Attacks).

When a Character gets a Contamination card (regardless of the source), draw it from the Contamination deck and place it on top of their Action discard pile.

Contamination cards are a disadvantage for the player, because they are kept in hand like a normal Action card, but they do not provide any additional Actions and you cannot spend them to pay the Costs of the other Actions.

Each Contamination card contains hidden information: the Character may be INFECTED or not. This information is hidden by colorful patterns in the text field. Unless the card is “Scanned”, this information remains unknown to the player until the end of the game.

If the Character does not Scan their Contamination cards before the end of the game, then at the end of the game they may lose the game because of these cards.

More on Victory Check – see Player’s Goals and End of the Game, page 11.  
Note: Some Event cards may force the player to Scan their Contamination cards.

# SCANNING AND REMOVING CONTAMINATION CARDS

A Character may try to get rid of their Contamination cards through several different ways (like the Rest Action card, a Canteen, Shower or Surgery Room Action and the Antidote Item Action).

Each card/Room description details the procedure to follow. Whatever the procedure, it requires a Scan of the Contamination cards. A Scan is performed in the following way:

## Victory check:

After Turn 5, the Shuttle leaves the Nemesis and goes back to the mothership regardless of the Characters on the Shuttle board.

In order to win the game in this mode, a player must fulfill the following requirements:

1. The players must have **revealed all the Discovery tokens** on the Nemesis.  
   o In a 2-player game, up to 3 Discovery tokens may remain unrevealed.  
   If this condition is not met, the mission is not successful - the players lose.

2. The player must **fulfill their Personal Requirement**.

3. The player’s Character **must be on the Shuttle board when the Shuttle goes back to the mothership** (or Character must leave the ship with an Escape Pod).

4. The players must resolve their **Contamination Check** (as in the base game).

**OR:**  
The player may also fulfill the **Lucrative Offer** at any time if they don’t want to help their crewmates: they must Send the Signal and escape with an Intruder Egg in an Escape Pod, which give them an automatic victory if they survive the Contamination Check.
